title: Who owned it, and how fast the cash went
lede: Pets.com raised about $188M in cash in under 20 months. Amazon was its largest owner. At the rate the company lost money, the tank never held more than about two quarters of runway.

blocks.title: The cap table after the IPO
blocks.subtitle: Beneficial ownership on 29,544,737 shares outstanding after the offering. Hover over or tap a holder.
blocks.source: 424B4 prospectus, principal stockholders table[^1]. Percentages are beneficial ownership and include exercisable options, so they don’t sum exactly. “IPO public float” (7.5M shares) and “All other holders” are derived. Catalyst Investments is a Disney affiliate. Before the IPO, Amazon held 40.7%.

blocks.caption: The runway countdown: cash at quarter end, and quarters of runway at that quarter’s loss rate (derived)

rows.text: Dec 31, 1999: **0.7 quarters** at the Q4 ’99 loss of $42.4M[^1]
Mar 31, 2000: **1.8 quarters** after the IPO, at the Q1 loss of $39.1M[^2]
Jun 30, 2000: **1.5 quarters** at the Q2 loss of $24.1M[^3]
Sep 30, 2000: **1.1 quarters** at the Q3 loss of $21.7M. Shut down 38 days later.[^4]

blocks.source: Runway (derived) = cash ÷ that quarter’s net loss. Net loss includes non-cash charges, so actual cash burn was somewhat lower.
